author: sonnet
label: c2-seed-sonnet-01
changes: Expanded the thin bullet notes into sections that say where each piece of state lives, what triggers each transition, and what happens on failure, as the brief asked.

Added a table of new state with its location (column, table or cookie), and explained how the account's 2FA state is derived from user_totp, which lets one table hold both the active and the pending secret.
Labelled every diagram transition with its trigger and added the missing failure and self-loop transitions (wrong code, wrong password, cancel replacement, 5 wrong entries or 5-minute expiry).

Replaced vague notes (drift tolerance, 'handled when enabled', re-authentication) with concrete rules: replay check via last_step with an atomic conditional update, other sessions deleted in the confirm transaction, disable needs password plus code.
Stated how a recovery-code sign-in leads straight to setting up a new authenticator: replacement needs no proof of the old one.
Spelled out that 2FA sign-in creates no session until the code passes, and that the p2f cookie stores a raw token whose hash is in pending_logins, mirroring sid.
Flagged an assumption the brief does not cover (rate limiting wrong codes during setup) for confirmation.
Kept the open question about users with no phone and no recovery codes marked open and undesigned.
Defined terms and stack pieces (seal, enqueue_email, start_session) inline so a reader new to the project can follow.
Defined TOTP and 'time step' for a reader new to the stack.

Fixed an inconsistency: start_session() was listed as reused unchanged, but it redirects to /home, while the doc needs a redirect to Security settings after a recovery-code sign-in. The doc now says the caller changes the redirect target and keeps the sid cookie.
Stated that every account-lifecycle action requires being signed in, once, instead of only under 'Start'.
Said the current session is identified by its sid cookie.
Clarified that wrong entries of either kind (authenticator or recovery code) count toward the 5 attempts.
Explained the replay check more plainly: the conditional UPDATE only applies if the new step is larger.
Noted that an abandoned setup is harmless because sign-in ignores the pending secret.
Marked the rate-limit proposal for the confirm endpoint explicitly as an assumption to confirm.
Clarified in the diagram intro where the sign-in attempt starts and ends.
Tightened wording throughout and used a plain list for the two code types in the intro.
Moved the definition of time step and RFC 6238 to a short section before the state table, so terms are explained before use, and explained that RFC 6238 is the standard TOTP algorithm.
Defined 'recovery code' in the opening list.
Clarified that start_session() sets sid and that only the redirect target changes after a recovery-code sign-in (removed the confusing 'kept as is' sentence).
Stated that the replay rule also applies to codes entered when confirming and disabling.
Simplified the authenticator-code step by removing the duplicated description of 6 digits and the time window, now covered in the definition.
Minor wording tightening throughout; structure, diagram and open question unchanged.
